title: Did a civilisation exist on Earth before humans?
speaker: BBC Learning English

sentences.en: Hello, this is 6 Minute English from BBC Learning English.
sentences.zh: 你好,这是6分钟英语 从英国广播公司学习英语。

sentences.en: I'm Beth. And I'm Phil. Phil, do you believe there's life on other planets?
sentences.zh: 我是贝丝 我是菲尔 菲尔 你相信其他星球上有生命吗

sentences.en: Well, there's a lot of other planets, so yeah, I think there must be.
sentences.zh: 嗯,有很多其他行星, 所以是的,我想一定有。

sentences.en: Yeah, I agree. Well, it's a question that interests American astrophysicist Adam Frank, who discussed it with his colleague Gavin Schmidt, director of Nasa's Institute for Space Studies.
sentences.zh: 是的,我同意,这是一个美国天体物理学家亚当·弗兰克感兴趣的问题, 他和他的同事加文·施密特讨论了这个问题, 纳萨空间研究所所长。

sentences.en: Here, Adam recalls their conversation for BBC World Service programme CrowdScience: We know that there's been no other civilisation on Earth, and he stopped me and said, "How do you know that?" And my jaw just dropped down to the floor.
sentences.zh: 在这里,亚当回忆了他们为英国广播公司世界服务节目CrowdScience的谈话: 我们知道地球上没有其它文明, 他阻止我说,“你怎么知道的?”我的下巴掉到地板上。

sentences.en: Adam's jaw dropped – an idiom for when someone looks shocked and surprised.
sentences.zh: 亚当的下巴掉下来了——当某人看起来震惊和惊讶时,他就是个白痴。

sentences.en: Could there have been a technologically advanced civilisation before us, here on Earth?
sentences.zh: 地球上是否曾有过一个技术先进的文明?

sentences.en: It may sound weird but this idea has a scientific name.
sentences.zh: 听起来可能有点怪 但这个想法有科学的名字

sentences.en: Here is Caroline Steel, presenter of BBC's CrowdScience, to explain: The Silurian hypothesis proposes that if there was a technologically advanced civilisation hundreds of millions of years ago, we wouldn't be able to find traces of it.
sentences.zh: 这是英国广播公司的Crowd Science的主持人Caroline Steel, 来解释:Silurian的假设是,如果在数亿年前有技术先进的文明, 我们就无法找到它的痕迹。

sentences.en: A hypothesis is an idea which explains how something happens and can be tested to find out if it's correct.
sentences.zh: 假设是一个解释事情发生方式的理念 并且可以测试它是否正确。

sentences.en: In this episode, we'll be discussing the Silurian hypothesis: the idea that a technologically advanced civilisation existed before us on Earth but vanished without leaving a trace.
sentences.zh: 在这个片段里,我们将讨论Silurian的假设: 一种技术先进的文明 存在于我们面前的想法, 却在没有留下痕迹的情况下消失了。

sentences.en: As usual, we'll be learning some useful new words and idioms, and remember – you'll find all the vocabulary on our website, bbclearningenglish.com.
sentences.zh: 与往常一样,我们会学习一些有用的新词和新语, 并记住——你会在我们的网站上找到所有的词汇,bbc学习英语。com。

sentences.en: But first, I have a question for you, Phil.
sentences.zh: 但首先 我有个问题要问你 菲尔

sentences.en: Human civilisation is thousands of years old but the planet itself is much older.
sentences.zh: 人类文明已存在数千年,但地球本身却更古老。

sentences.en: So, how old do scientists think the Earth is?
sentences.zh: 那么,科学家们认为地球有多老?

sentences.en: Is it: a) 3.5 billion years, b) 4.5 billion years, or c) 5.5 billion years?
sentences.zh: 是:(a) 35亿年,(b) 45亿年,还是(c) 55亿年?

sentences.en: I'm going to guess c) 5.5 billion years.
sentences.zh: 我想是的,(c) 55亿年。

sentences.en: OK. Well, we will find the answer out later in the programme.
sentences.zh: 好吧,我们稍后会在节目中找到答案

sentences.en: To believe a technologically advanced civilisation existed on Earth hundreds of millions of years ago, most people would probably want evidence.
sentences.zh: 相信在数亿年前 地球上存在一个技术先进的文明, 大多数人可能想要证据。

sentences.en: We have evidence about other species from the past, such as the dinosaurs, from fossils – the remains of prehistoric plants or animals that have been preserved in rock for a very long time.
sentences.zh: 我们有关于过去其他物种的证据,例如恐龙,来自化石——史前植物或动物的残骸,在岩石中保存了很长时间。

sentences.en: But according to Adam Frank, fossils won't help prove the Silurian hypothesis, as he explains here to BBC World Service programme, CrowdScience: Most things are not fossilised.
sentences.zh: 但据Adam Frank说 化石无法证明Silurian的假设 正如他在BBC世界服务节目《人群科学》中解释的那样: 大部分东西没有化石化。

sentences.en: It's only a tiny fraction of Earth's life that has ever become fossilised.
sentences.zh: 地球生命中只有一小部分 已经化石化了

sentences.en: So, imagine that you have a 10,000-year-long civilisation, which is a blink of the eye for geology – that's too short to really create a lot of fossils.
sentences.zh: 想象一下,你有一个长达一万年的文明, 也就是地质学的眨眼—— 这太短了,无法创造出很多化石。

sentences.en: Adam argues that only a tiny fraction – meaning a very small amount – of life on Earth has turned into fossil.
sentences.zh: 亚当认为,地球上生命中只有一小部分 — — 也就是很小一部分 — — 变成了化石。

sentences.en: In geological time, even a 10,000-year-old civilisation is the blink of an eye – an idiom meaning a very short period of time.
sentences.zh: 在地质学时代,即使是一万年的文明化,也是眼的眨眼,这种奇观意味着很短的时间。

sentences.en: In other words, older civilisations might have existed on Earth but not for long enough to leave fossilised evidence.
sentences.zh: 换句话说,古老的文明可能存在于地球上,但还不足以留下化石化的证据。

sentences.en: However, not everyone is convinced by Adam's ideas.
sentences.zh: 但是,并非每个人都相信亚当的想法。

sentences.en: Evidence of our own civilisation, including plastics and man-made materials like concrete, is already being layered into the Earth's crust, and these are going to last a very long time.
sentences.zh: 我们自身文明的证据,包括塑料和混凝土等人造材料, 已经被埋入地壳, 并且它们会持续很长一段时间。

sentences.en: So, surely a technologically advanced civilisation from prehistory would have left similar marks.
sentences.zh: 因此,从史前的先进技术文明 肯定会留下相似的痕迹。

sentences.en: Well, here's Adam Frank again, answering these objections on BBC World Service programme, CrowdScience: What happens is somebody else will pick up on their work, either affirming it and showing new evidence for it or pushing back on it, and once you get to, like, 20, 30 or 40 papers, then you have a consensus.You're like, "OK.
sentences.zh: Adam Frank再次回答 BBC World Science 节目的反对意见:Crowd Science: 发生的事情是,其他人会接听他们的作品, 要么确认它,展示新的证据,要么推倒它, 一旦你拿到了20,30或40份文件, 然后你就达成了共识。你就会说,“好吧。

sentences.en: We've really, really looked at this and now we know."
sentences.zh: 我们真的,真的 看看这个,现在我们知道了。"

sentences.en: Adam welcomes new evidence, even evidence which contradicts his ideas, as part of the scientific method needed to prove a hypothesis right or wrong.
sentences.zh: 亚当欢迎新的证据,甚至与他的想法相矛盾的证据,作为证明一种假设对错所需的科学方法的一部分。

sentences.en: It's how scientists form a consensus – meaning a general agreement – about the issue.
sentences.zh: 这就是科学家如何就这一问题形成共识,即达成普遍共识。

sentences.en: Personally, I think the idea of prehistoric civilisations on Earth is so mysterious, it's OK to keep an open mind.
sentences.zh: 就个人而言,我认为史前文明在地球上的理念 是如此的神秘, 保持开放的心态是正常的。

sentences.en: Now, isn't it time you revealed the answer to your question, Beth?
sentences.zh: 现在,是不是该你 透露你的问题的答案,贝丝?

sentences.en: I think it is. I asked you, "How old do scientists think the Earth is?" You said, "5.5 billion years," and I'm afraid you were wrong, Phil.
sentences.zh: 我想是的,我问你,“科学家们认为地球有多老?” 你说,“55亿年”,恐怕你错了,菲尔。

sentences.en: It's 4.5 billion years. OK. Let's recap the vocabulary we've learnt, starting with the idiom my jaw dropped, which is used to say someone looks very shocked and surprised.
sentences.zh: 这是45亿年。好吧。让我们回顾一下我们学到的词汇, 从我的下巴掉下来的语气开始, 常说有人看起来非常震惊和惊讶。

sentences.en: A hypothesis is a suggestion that's proposed to explain something, which can then be tested to see if it's true.
sentences.zh: 假设是一个建议 解释的东西, 然后可以测试 看它是否真实。

sentences.en: Fossils are the remains of prehistoric plants or animals that have been preserved in rock for a very long time.
sentences.zh: 化石是史前植物或动物的残骸 已经保存在岩石中很长时间了

sentences.en: A tiny fraction of something is a very small amount of it.
sentences.zh: 很小的一部分东西是很小的一部分。

sentences.en: The idiom the blink of an eye means a very short period of time.
sentences.zh: 眼睛眨一眨意味着时间很短

sentences.en: And finally, a consensus is a general agreement.
sentences.zh: 最后,协商一致是一项普遍协议。

sentences.en: Once again, our six minutes are up, but if you're keen for more, then head over to our website, bbclearningenglish.com, where you'll find a worksheet and a quiz for this episode.
sentences.zh: 再一次,我们的六分钟到了, 但如果你热衷于更多, 那么去我们的网站,bbclearingenglish.com, 在那里你会找到一个工作表和这个插曲的测验。

sentences.en: See you again soon. But for now, it's goodbye!
sentences.zh: 很快再见,但现在再见了!

sentences.en: Goodbye!
sentences.zh: 再见!
